target_customer: Retailers and e-commerce companies running text marketing and text-based checkout
problem: Retailers wanted to sell and market via text message. Locent offered a white-label text marketing suite with automatic campaigns and purchases by a single text keyword or emoji.
business_model: B2B SaaS with billing for active subscribers only
product_category: SMS marketing and conversational commerce platform

founders.name: Matt Joseph
founders.background_notes: Per YC page bio. Education not found.

competitors.name: Magic
competitors.what: Startup selling products and services through messaging, named by Locent's press release
competitors.funding_then: Tens of millions raised across Magic and Operator per the release

competitors.name: Operator
competitors.what: Startup selling products and services through messaging, named by Locent's press release
competitors.funding_then: Tens of millions raised across Magic and Operator per the release

technical_complexity.rationale: Required carrier-grade SMS delivery, opt-out handling, an API and a text payments flow, with campaign generation using customer context.

defensibility.rationale: SMS infrastructure was available from vendors and features such as automated campaigns were copyable. The subscriber guarantee was a pricing differentiator, not a moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Messaging commerce rivals were well funded; no source found on any acquisition of Locent.

market_need_then: The February 2016 release said retailers and e-commerce companies were adopting conversational commerce, but no customer count or revenue was disclosed.

branding.domain_note: Used locent.com per the YC page

identity.voice_and_tone: StackShare tagline: build a full text marketing program in minutes without writing any copy or code

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by TechCrunch and a YC blog post at launch but no press about the brand itself; Product Hunt shows unrelated products sharing the name.

outcome_analysis: Locent, a text marketing platform for retailers, raised seed money from Chaac Ventures in June 2015 and added YC and Mike Benvenuti for 750 thousand dollars in total by February 2016. It is now listed as inactive by YC and dead by CB Insights, with 870 thousand dollars reported raised, but no shutdown announcement or acquisition was found, so the cause is not public.
notes: locent.com failed DNS resolution, so the site is treated as dead or unreachable. The press release states a total of $750K but no amount for the individual rounds, so amounts are null. CB Insights reports $870K total raised, about $120K more than the press release, which suggests a missing round (possibly the YC investment) that rests on a single database and is unresolved. The Chaac round date rests on a search result for the GlobeNewswire release and was not opened. The YC blog post of 2015-08-03 quotes TechCrunch naming Ryan MacInnes alongside Matt Joseph but does not call him a co-founder, so he is not recorded. Competitor sources are dated 2016-02, about six months after the batch, kept with that caveat.
